title: Chip Stocks Sell Off as Traders Price In Tougher AI Rules and Slower Data-Center Builds
dek: AMD, Nvidia and Intel fell after the midterms raised the prospect of tighter AI rules and slower data-center construction, even though AMD had just posted a record quarter.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Early graphics processor chip from Nvidia's NV1 family

keyPoints: AMD fell about 13% in morning trading to $424.36, Nvidia about 7% and Intel about 8%, per 24/7 Wall St, days after AMD reported record Q3 revenue of $13.38 billion.
StockTitan's midday data showed Nvidia down 7.49% and AMD down 15.17% at 12:04 p.m. ET, with Micron down 13.67%; the Nasdaq Composite was 3.9% lower at 11:49 a.m. ET, in a correction, per CNBC.
The selloff follows Democrats' midterm wins in both chambers. Rep. Yassamin Ansari, a Democrat, called on Nov. 4 for a pause on advanced AI development until adequate regulations are in place.
Reuters, cited by TipRanks, reported UBS analysts' view that about 30% of expected U.S. data-center capacity additions in 2028 could face risks from potential construction pauses.
No AI bill has passed. The fear is about what a Democratic Congress could do from January, not about rules already in force.
body:
Chip stocks fell again on Thursday, extending Wednesday's losses, as investors priced in the possibility that a Democratic Congress and state officials could tighten the rules that govern AI data centers. The move is about what could slow AI spending, not about a weak quarter. AMD had just reported its largest and most profitable quarter in company history.

## The numbers

AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.38 billion, up 44.7% from a year earlier and ahead of the $13.08 billion consensus. Its Data Center revenue rose 97% to $8.55 billion. The company guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%.

That did not protect the stock. 24/7 Wall St reported AMD at $424.36, down 13% in morning trading. StockTitan's midday data put AMD down 15.17% and Nvidia down 7.49%. Micron, another AI-trade name, was down 13.67%.

The broader market reflected the same worry. CNBC reported the Nasdaq Composite down 3.9% at 11:49 a.m. ET, more than 10% below its record from last month, a correction. The S&P 500 was down 2.8%.

## The policy fear

The trigger is the election. Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterms. Rep. Yassamin Ansari called on Nov. 4 for a pause on advanced AI development until adequate regulations are in place, according to 24/7 Wall St. A pause resolution is not law, and there is no federal AI bill on the table yet that would stop data-center construction.

Still, investors are pricing the risk. Reuters reported that UBS analysts estimate about 30% of expected U.S. data-center capacity additions in 2028 could face risk from potential construction pauses, as cited by TipRanks. State-level pressure is a second channel: a Colorado legislative staff report, cited by 24/7, noted that states have enacted a range of legislation and executive orders on data centers, covering energy use, water and electricity costs.

## Company-specific pressure

Qualcomm's weak handset sales added to the pressure on chip names. Its handset revenue fell 26% year over year to $5.14 billion, and TipRanks noted the concern that falling phone demand could eventually reach the wider semiconductor group. Intel, which had already slid on weak guidance from its Oct. 29 earnings report, fell about 8% in the 24/7 report.

AMD chief executive Lisa Su said on the earnings call that the company now expects revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027, more than twice its long-term model. The market has not yet accepted that outlook as a reason to hold the stock through the policy scare.

## What to watch

The timing matters. A new Congress is not sworn in until January, and any AI rule would need to clear a presidential veto and the Senate filibuster. The near-term risk is that committee hearings and state actions shape spending plans before any law exists. Investors will look at the next round of data-center capacity guidance from hyperscalers and chip makers for evidence that projects are being delayed, not just discussed.

marketImpact.summary: The selloff is driven by policy risk to data-center build-outs rather than by a fall in reported demand. AMD's record quarter and Q4 guidance argue for a rebound if no rules move; a real construction pause would hit the whole AI accelerator chain.
marketImpact.timeframe: Next few sessions, then the January Congress start and any state data-center actions

catalysts.event: Chip stocks fall on midterm-driven AI regulation fears; Nasdaq Composite in correction at midday per CNBC
AMD's fourth-quarter guidance of about $17 billion, and any change to its 2027 outlook, is the next company-level test

tickers.rationale: Fell about 13-15% intraday after a beat-and-raise quarter; the drop is about policy and build pace, not the reported results
Down about 7% intraday on the same data-center policy fear; also exposed to the China import hold on H200 chips
Down about 8% on the sector selloff, following weak guidance from its own earnings last month
Handset revenue fell 26% year over year; the stock was down about 12% in premarket trading on the results
